context.why: Stories 1 to 3 are accepted. /api/v1/people/ and /api/v1/organizations/ serve a list entry and a fuller single record (PersonSerializer, OrganizationSerializer in fairdm/api/serializers.py), each with its filter set in fairdm/api/filters.py. ProjectViewSet and DatasetViewSet in fairdm/api/viewsets.py have no filter set of their own yet. This last story lets a script go from a contributor to their work: a `contributor` filter on the project list and the dataset list, and the addresses of those two narrowed lists on a single person and a single organization.
spec_sections: Clarifications (how a script finds what a person or organization is credited on)
Edge Cases (a person credited on a private record the caller may see)
prior_decisions: decisions.md D6 and D8: the narrowed list holds the records the contributor is CREDITED on and that are PUBLIC, for every caller. Credit only: `contributor.projects.get_visible()` and `contributor.datasets.get_visible()` (Contributor.projects / .datasets in fairdm/contrib/contributors/models.py around line 350, and the base Contributor.get_public_projects/get_public_datasets, which do exactly this). Do NOT call get_public_projects()/get_public_datasets() on the real instance: Organization overrides both to add projects it owns, and an owned project with no credit must not be returned (T020 tests this).

Public only for every caller means the narrowed list ignores the levels a caller holds: a member of a private dataset's team asking for ?contributor=<person> does not get that private dataset, although the plain dataset list would show it to them. FairDMVisibilityFilter still runs on the viewset; the contributor filter intersects with it, so the result is the public credited records.

ContributorRecordsFilterSet in fairdm/api/filters.py with one filter, `contributor`, a CharFilter with a method (not a ModelChoiceFilter: an unknown identifier must give an empty list with status 200, never a 400). The method looks the contributor up by uuid among Person.objects.real() and Organization.objects.all(); when nobody matches (an unknown value, a superuser's or the anonymous account's uuid, a database number) it returns queryset.none(). It narrows by primary key: queryset.filter(pk__in=<credited visible records>.values('pk')). Check that get_visible() exists on both the project and the dataset querysets and what it means for a dataset in a private project (it must be left out).

One class serves both lists: it picks projects or datasets from the queryset's model. Set it as filterset_class on ProjectViewSet and DatasetViewSet. Read FairDMFilterBackend.get_filterset_class first: it combines the view's filterset_class with ChangedSinceFilterSet and builds a Meta when there is none, so a filter set whose Meta names no model has to work for both. PersonFilterSet and OrganizationFilterSet show how stories 2 and 3 fitted in.

T021: PersonSerializer and OrganizationSerializer each gain exactly two fields, `projects` and `datasets`: the absolute address of the project list and the dataset list with ?contributor=<uuid>, built with rest_framework.reverse.reverse and the request from the serializer context (the path alone when there is no request, as the other address fields do). They are on the single record only, not on the list entries. No query is spent on them.

The existing test in story 2 and story 3 that pins the exact key set of a single person and a single organization (TestPerson, TestOrganization, and the schema tests in tests/test_api/test_schema.py) will need the two new keys added. Those are tests of this feature written by earlier stories of it: extend their expected key sets, change nothing else in them, and name each such edit in progress.md.
The query-count tests for project and dataset lists (TestQueryCount, TestCreditQueries) must stay green with the filter unused and should not grow when it is used.

T023: docs/portal-development/restful-api.md gains the `contributor` filter under the filters section with an example for a person and one for an organization, the sentence that it returns public records only whoever asks, and the two addresses in the People and Organizations field tables. docs/user-guide/reading-records-with-a-script.md gains a short worked step from a person to their datasets. Name ContributorRecordsFilterSet in the developer page.
